name: Question 5
problem: At which point on the surface $z=3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ is the tangent plane perpendicular to the vector  $v=⟨4,-2,-1⟩?$
worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}),
$$

where $⟨\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}),\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}),-1⟩$ represents a normal vector to the tangent plane.

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})=6x \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2})=2y\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the normal vector to the tangent plane is 

$$
⟨6x,\,2y,\,-1⟩.
$$

Our tangent plane should be perpendicular to $⟨4,-2,-1⟩.$ So, the normal vector of that plane must be parallel to that vector. In other words, for some constant $c$, we must have

$$
c\cdot ⟨6x,\,2y,\,-1⟩=⟨4,-2,-1⟩.
$$

Equating the corresponding coordinates, we obtain the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}6cx=4 \\ 2cy=-2 \\ -c=-1\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get $c=1.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
6(1)x=4\,⟹\,x=\frac{2}{3}.
$$

And substituting $c=1$ into the second equation, we have 

$$
2(1)y=-2\,⟹\,y=-1.
$$

Finally, substituting $x=\frac{2}{3}$ and $y=-1$ into our function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =3{(\frac{2}{3})}^{2}+(-1)^{2} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}+1 \\  & =\frac{7}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangent plane is perpendicular to the vector $v$ at $(\frac{2}{3},-1,\frac{7}{3}).$

Question 5
?

At which point on the surface z=3x2+y2 is the tangent plane perpendicular to the vector v=⟨4,−2,−1⟩?

a
(23,−1,73)
b
(1,0,3)
c
(−13,0,19)
d
(0,1,1)
e
(−1,−1,4)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface z=f(x,y) at the point (x0,y0,z0) on the surface can be written as z−z0=(x−x0)∂f∂x(x0,y0)+(y−y0)∂f∂y(x0,y0), where ⟨∂f∂x(x0,y0),∂f∂y(x0,y0),−1⟩ represents a normal vector to the tangent plane.

First, we find the partial derivatives: ∂f∂x=∂∂x(3x2+y2)=6x∂f∂y=∂∂y(3x2+y2)=2y

Hence, the normal vector to the tangent plane is ⟨6x,2y,−1⟩.

Our tangent plane should be perpendicular to ⟨4,−2,−1⟩. So, the normal vector of that plane must be parallel to that vector. In other words, for some constant c, we must have c⋅⟨6x,2y,−1⟩=⟨4,−2,−1⟩.

Equating the corresponding coordinates, we obtain the following system: {6cx=42cy=−2−c=−1

From the third equation, we get c=1. Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain 6(1)x=4⟹x=23.

And substituting c=1 into the second equation, we have 2(1)y=−2⟹y=−1.

Finally, substituting x=23 and y=−1 into our function, we get z=3(23)2+(−1)2=43+1=73.

Therefore, the tangent plane is perpendicular to the vector v at (23,−1,73).
